summary: WorldEntity primary PR #293 correctly safe-bounds lifecycle revisions but still accepts origin.generatorVersion above IEEE-754's exact integer range. cloneOrigin validates generatorVersion only as finite, >=1, and integral, so 9007199254740992 can enter frozen canonical generation provenance even though adjacent integers above 2^53-1 are not uniquely representable. Generator version is part of the version lock/provenance boundary and should remain exact plain data.
evidence: PR #293 exact head 093f2f6016427753647a00d2ea85c55ed7ce9ffa defines MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and applies it to stateRevision, representationRevision, and duplicate diagnostic capacity.
The same head's cloneOrigin obtains origin.generatorVersion through checkedFiniteNumber and checks only >= 1 plus math.floor equality; it has no MAX_SAFE_INTEGER bound.

Docs/ARCHITECTURE.md defines generation origin as generator name/version and first-observation version information as canonical truth that must prevent later generator upgrades from silently rewriting established reality.

Because Luau numbers are doubles, integer provenance above 9007199254740991 cannot preserve one-to-one adjacent integer identity; max-safe acceptance plus max-safe+1 rejection should be regression-locked.
